Explanation: The core value unit is a product listing: a seller makes an offer discoverable through Flipkart by combining product information, price, availability and a delivery promise.
Flipkart owns and orchestrates the marketplace experience. Walmart's FY2026 SEC filing lists Flipkart Private Limited as an 84%-owned significant subsidiary.
Flipkart's job is to connect demand and supply while making the full transaction reliable enough to scale across India.
More shoppers attract more sellers and assortment; more supply improves selection and creates transaction, advertising and service monetization opportunities.
Scale increases the burden of seller quality, fraud, counterfeit control, regulatory compliance, fulfillment reliability and customer experience.
Flipkart orchestrates discovery, checkout, marketplace fees, seller settlements and supporting services around each transaction.
Transaction Flows: ← Provider · Listing / Fees — Sellers supply product listings and participate under the marketplace fee and policy structure. | → Consumer · Discovery — Flipkart makes seller offers searchable, comparable and recommendable through one customer interface. | ← Consumer · Order / Pay — The shopper places the marketplace order and pays through Flipkart's checkout experience. | → Provider · Payout — Flipkart coordinates seller settlement after the order, net of applicable fees and adjustments. | → Partner · Shipment — The platform and its logistics layer route delivery work into the physical fulfillment network.

Explanation: The platform governs seller onboarding, product compliance, marketplace integrity, reviews, fraud controls, service standards and enforcement.
Flipkart uses its app, web experience, search and recommendation systems, advertising and large shopping events such as The Big Billion Days to activate demand.
Flipkart recruits sellers, structures listings, matches supply with demand, governs participation, coordinates payments and fulfillment, and operates the customer experience.
Key resources include the Flipkart brand and commerce stack, marketplace data and algorithms, Seller Hub, payments capabilities and the Flipkart Group's Ekart logistics infrastructure.
Consumers across India use Flipkart to discover, compare and buy products from third-party sellers through one marketplace experience.
Shoppers want to find and purchase the right product without searching across many separate sellers or managing fulfillment themselves.
A large assortment, price competition, shopping events, payment options, returns and national delivery can increase convenience and perceived value.
Counterfeits, poor seller quality, failed delivery, returns friction or weak service can undermine confidence in a large marketplace.
Shoppers place orders and pay through Flipkart's commerce experience while the underlying product is supplied by a marketplace seller.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Discovery — Flipkart makes seller offers searchable, comparable and recommendable through one customer interface. | → Owner · Order / Pay — The shopper places the marketplace order and pays through Flipkart's checkout experience. | ← Partner · Delivery — Logistics partners complete the physical last mile and support reverse flows such as returns.

Explanation: The transaction depends on account, product and geographic serviceability as well as fraud, payment and category restrictions.
Shoppers primarily access the marketplace through Flipkart's mobile app and website.
They search, compare, order, pay, receive products, return items when necessary and contribute reviews or other trust signals.
Consumers contribute attention, purchase intent, account and payment details, delivery information and behavioral data.
Third-party sellers, brands, MSMEs and entrepreneurs provide the assortment sold through the marketplace rather than Flipkart owning all of that inventory.
Sellers use Flipkart to reach national demand without building an equivalent consumer marketplace and distribution interface themselves.
Sellers gain access to large-scale demand plus seller tools, advertising, fulfillment, insights and shopping-event visibility.
Sellers face marketplace fees, price and visibility competition, compliance requirements, returns and service-performance pressure.
Sellers create offers, maintain inventory and fulfill marketplace demand directly or with Flipkart-supported fulfillment and logistics.

Explanation: Seller access is governed through business verification, tax and bank details, product rules, marketplace policies and ongoing performance controls.
Seller Hub and related tools let sellers onboard, create listings, manage orders, inventory, payments, advertising and support.
Sellers list products, manage price and inventory, process orders, prepare shipments, advertise and manage customer outcomes.
They contribute the inventory, catalogue data, prices, product images, seller credentials and operational capacity that create marketplace supply.

Independent delivery partners and franchise operators extend the physical network around Flipkart's marketplace. Ekart itself is treated here as a Flipkart Group resource, while external operators sit in the Partner role.
Their job is to extend reliable pickup, line-haul and last-mile capacity across India's highly varied geography.
Marketplace and Ekart shipment volume creates recurring delivery demand and commercial opportunity for logistics partners.
Festive peaks, difficult addresses, remote geographies, service-level expectations and high last-mile variability make execution difficult.
Partners execute logistics work and receive compensation through their delivery or franchise relationships.

Explanation: Participation depends on geography, capacity, operational standards, service levels and integration with the logistics network.
Partners connect operationally through Ekart's delivery and franchise network, local hubs, technology and contractual arrangements.
Partners pick up, route and deliver shipments, handle exceptions and support reverse logistics.
They contribute vehicles, delivery capacity, local knowledge, operating staff and geographic reach.
